one_question: Must an integrated complex organ evolve as an integrated unit?
working_answer: Phenotypic integration can be repeatedly reconstructed from components whose coupling is not persistently shared across ecology, history and genomic inheritance.
rejected_or_demoted_framings: ecological modules necessarily align with genomic modules
combinatorial reuse alone is the Nature-scale novelty
accelerated evolutionary rate is a prerequisite for the main mechanism

competing_models.fixed_evolutionary_integration: present phenotype modules persist as shared genomic/local-history units
competing_models.reconfigurable_integration: present phenotype integration coexists with separable component genomic histories and recombinant reassembly

nature_kill_shot: Natural or segregating genomic mosaics independently predict component states/new capitulum combinations while preserving a coherent integrated reproductive phenotype.
primary_falsifier: All focal components follow the same local genomic ancestry and phenotype combinations track one inseparable genomic background.
figure_contract: Fig1: present integration plus failure of one fixed ecological partition and robust component-specific ecological anchors
Fig2: repeated, unequal-depth, nonsynchronized component histories
Fig3: same-individual test of genomic co-inheritance versus separable local histories
Fig4: natural genomic reassembly and prospective/out-of-sample combination prediction
Fig5: representative function-to-fitness chain showing coherent reproductive performance after component reassembly
claim_boundaries: cross-level modularity mismatch is not itself claimed as unprecedented
historical nonsynchrony is not genetic independence
genomic modularity requires same-individual dense data and reference-stable inference
species-wide state multiplicity is not a verified within-population combinatorial substrate
